title: Through his eyes
rule: Every panel is the agent's own view: his hands and pencil are seen, never his face; the stranger is heard and glimpsed through the glass.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p65_through_his_eyes.py (lit cards and set pieces: p28_dealt_cards.py -> 99-ways-subjective lightbox.py, e4.py)
made: eight lit paper cards (p28_dealt_cards.Card: the 99-ways-subjective lamp-lit fibrous sheet, set pieces cut sharp against it) laid square two by four on the lightbox felt board, each the agent's own view

his hands: the 99-ways-subjective scissor-cut RightHand rig behind the sheet (soft body and penumbra), in pinch and reach poses; his left hand the same rig cut mirror-wise; his pencil a cut bar through the pinch
his spectacles: the outer arcs of two lens rims and the bridge, a cut card nearer the lamp, falling as a soft out-of-focus shadow across the top of every card (the eyes the page looks through)
the stranger only heard and glimpsed: her balloons come from beyond the TICKET OFFICE glass; her figure (b1m2 stranger bust) held back behind the glass as soft grey
the four canon lines in the shared cut-paper balloons; his own two lines tailed off the bottom edge of the card, toward his unseen mouth
the ANRC 1922 key cutout as the key on its hook (p28.key_on_hook), SERVICE tag slip; folio '65 / Through his eyes' (pen99.folio)

events.E0: 1: the memo held in his left hand, pencil at the 4:15 line; 2: his two hands push up from the desk edge, the cupboard and SERVICE door ahead
events.E1: 3: the ticket window, her shape soft beyond the glass: 'Pardon me — have you the right time?'
events.E2: 4: he looks up, pencil toward the clock at 4:10: 'Ten past four, by the clock.' (tail to below the frame: his mouth)
events.E3: 5: she turns from the glass: 'Much obliged!'; 6: the cupboard grows ahead, his hand reaching
events.E4: 7: his hand swings the leaf open on the left jamb: the key on its hook, tagged SERVICE
events.E5: 8: key unmoved, SERVICE door shut; his pencil hand rises out of the bottom of the frame (to his chin): 'Well, here I am... and what for?'

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: one view, his eyes on the cupboard: his hand reaches, swings the leaf open in steps until the key hangs in view, then the hand drops and the pencil rises out of the frame to his chin, and the line comes
beat_frames: b01: cupboard shut, his hand at the leaf
b03: leaf two thirds open, key showing
b04: open, key on its hook, hand on the leaf edge
b06: pencil up out of frame, the line

self_check.agent_figure_drawn: hands, cuffs, sleeves and pencil only; spectacle rims as near shadow
self_check.stranger: heard (balloons from beyond the glass) and glimpsed soft grey behind the TICKET OFFICE glass
self_check.check: A reader names whose eyes these are; the agent's face never appears.
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
